record.deltaSub: Free plan email sends a month
record.short: Free plan email sends cut from 2,000 to 300 a month; Starter’s 5x-contact-tier send limit replaced by shared HubSpot Credits.
record.headline: HubSpot cut the Free plan’s monthly marketing email sends from 2,000 to 300 and moved Starter’s email sending onto its shared Credits pool.
rows: Free, marketing email sends per month
5x marketing contact tier email send limit/month
record.who: Free users who send marketing email, and Starter customers whose email sends now count against Credits.
record.read: Cutting free sends this hard makes the free plan a trial of email marketing rather than a usable tool, which pushes active senders to Starter. Putting Starter’s sends on Credits means email now competes with other credit-spending actions, so heavy senders may hit a wall sooner than a fixed cap suggested.
record.caveat: The page doesn’t say how many Credits one email send uses, so the real Starter allowance can’t be compared with the old limit.

record.headline: xAI retired its SuperGrok plans and rebuilt Grok pricing as a ladder from $8 to $200 a month, with Cursor coding tools bundled in.
rows: SuperGrok Lite, SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy, Business
Free, Plus, Premium, Super, Ultra, Teams
record.who: Every Grok subscriber: the old SuperGrok plans are gone, so existing subscribers land on or must choose one of the new tiers.
record.read: An $8 entry tier lowers the price of getting into paid Grok, while the 50x Ultra tier at $200 targets heavy coding-agent users. Bundling Cursor features into every tier suggests xAI wants to sell Grok as a coding subscription as much as a chatbot.
record.caveat: The saved text doesn’t give the old SuperGrok prices, so the change for any one subscriber can’t be measured. PricingSaaS says the same lineup appears on Cursor’s pricing page.

record.short: Annual Grow shown at $89 instead of $79 and Advanced at $359 instead of $299 on Oct 15; back to $79 and $299 on Oct 16.
record.headline: Shopify showed higher annual Grow and Advanced prices for one day and then went back, which looks like a price test, not a decided rise.

record.read: Testing a rise only on annual billing suggests Shopify is checking whether committed merchants will accept a higher price. If one arm sticks, Advanced moves the most.
record.caveat: PricingSaaS saw the higher prices in one capture only and reads the reversal as an A/B arm flipping back; the current page shows $79 and $299.
